main_message: Three-site pathway comparison linking pristine Co32 Al-modified neighboring Co7 and Al47 control
Al strongly suppresses the Co-centered total population response while substantial O-centered oxidation response remains
Pristine shows stronger Co-centered local-spin relaxation while Al substitution is accompanied by stronger O-centered spin reorganization
Hirshfeld alpha and beta population changes resolve how the Co and O local-spin responses are constructed
Co+adsorbate localization is favored over Co-only hole localization and Al raises the valid Co-only M+2 penalty at *O
Across *OH *O and *OOH Co+adsorbate constraints remain lower in penalty than Co-only localization
Validated bonding analysis supports the origin of altered Co-O response
Matched charge-density-difference slices complement the cDFT response
Matched magnetization and spin-resolved maps support the spin-reorganization interpretation
Frontier-state character supports the bonding mechanism without raw-band-index claims
Net Bader electron loss is concentrated on adsorbate O while active-Co net-charge changes remain small
Active-Co 3d centroid shifts provide a compact spin-resolved spectral-response descriptor while framework-average shifts remain small
Replacing neighboring Co by Al removes nearly all near-EF neighbor-site frontier spectral weight
Independent Mulliken and Loewdin populations confirm strong spin-selective adsorbate-O redistribution with a smaller active-Co response
